title: Observability Stack
summary: Observability means being able to ask why production is misbehaving without shipping new code. Services emit three kinds of signal: metrics (cheap numbers over time), logs (detailed events), and traces (one request's path across services), all tagged with the same trace ID. Collectors process and route each signal to a store suited to it. Alerts on metrics wake someone up, and they pivot from a spike to the traces and logs that explain it.

walkthrough.title: Instrument and emit
walkthrough.text: Each service's OpenTelemetry SDK records request metrics, structured logs, and trace spans, and stamps the current trace_id on all three. A collector agent on each node receives them, batches, adds Kubernetes labels, and drops noisy data.

walkthrough.title: Metrics to a time-series DB
walkthrough.text: Counters and histograms (requests, errors, latency buckets) are written as time series. Each unique label combination is a separate series, so labels must stay low-cardinality.

walkthrough.title: Logs to a log store
walkthrough.text: Structured JSON logs are indexed by a few labels and compressed. Full-text search runs over a time range rather than over everything.

walkthrough.title: Traces, tail-sampled
walkthrough.text: The collector waits for a trace to finish, then keeps all errors and slow traces plus a small sample of normal ones, which cuts storage by about 90% without losing the interesting ones.

walkthrough.title: Evaluate alert rules
walkthrough.text: Alert rules run every 30 seconds against metrics, for example 'checkout error budget burning 14× faster than allowed over 1 h and 5 m'. Rules based on SLOs catch real user pain, not every blip.

walkthrough.title: Page the on-call
walkthrough.text: The firing alert is deduplicated and grouped, routed to the owning team's rotation, and links to a runbook and dashboard.

walkthrough.title: Pivot to the cause
walkthrough.text: On the latency graph, an exemplar dot links to a slow trace. The trace shows the payment call took 4 s, and its trace_id pulls up that request's logs, which contain the error.

data.label: Instrumented Services

output.name: Signals
output.type: Metrics, JSON logs, spans: all with trace_id

responsibilities: Emit the key signals: request rate, errors, duration, saturation.
Propagate trace context across HTTP, gRPC, and message queues.
Log structured events, not free text.

failureModes.scenario: User ID used as a metric label
failureModes.impact: Millions of series; the metrics DB runs out of memory.
failureModes.mitigation: Cardinality limits in the SDK and collector; IDs belong in logs and traces.

failureModes.scenario: Context not propagated through a queue
failureModes.mitigation: Inject trace context into message headers; test with end-to-end traces.

data.label: OTel Collectors

output.name: Routed
output.type: Each signal to its backend, enriched and filtered

responsibilities: Buffers and batches so services never block on telemetry.
Adds metadata (pod, node, region) and removes secrets and PII.
Samples traces after they complete and drops debug logs in production.

failureModes.impact: Telemetry dropped exactly during the incident.
failureModes.mitigation: Disk-backed queues; prioritise errors and metrics over debug data.
Non-blocking SDK exporters that drop rather than block; scale collectors on queue depth.

data.label: Metrics TSDB
responsibilities: Stores numeric time series cheaply with high compression.
Answers aggregate queries over days in milliseconds.
Serves as the source for alerts and SLO tracking.

failureModes.impact: Ingest rejected or OOM; dashboards go blank.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-tenant series limits and alerting on series growth.

failureModes.impact: p99 pain invisible behind a fine mean.
failureModes.mitigation: Histograms and percentile SLOs, not averages.

data.label: Log Store

output.name: Search
output.type: Filter by labels + text over a time range

responsibilities: Keeps detailed events for debugging and audit.
Indexes cheaply (labels) and scans contents when needed.
Finds every log line for one trace_id.

failureModes.mitigation: Sampling for verbose logs, retention tiers, and per-team quotas.

failureModes.scenario: Secrets or PII written to logs
failureModes.mitigation: Redaction in the collector; structured logging with safe fields.

data.label: Alerting & Paging

input.name: Rules
input.type: SLO burn-rate expressions evaluated every 30 s

responsibilities: Evaluates alert rules and deduplicates firing alerts.
Routes to the owning team's rotation with escalation.
Supports silences during maintenance.

failureModes.impact: Too many noisy pages, so real ones are ignored.
failureModes.mitigation: Alert on symptoms (SLO burn), not causes; review every page.
A dead man's switch heartbeat to an external service; run monitoring separately.

data.label: Trace Store
responsibilities: Stores request paths across dozens of services.
Shows where time went and which hop failed.
Links metrics exemplars to concrete example traces.

failureModes.scenario: Head sampling drops the interesting traces
failureModes.impact: The one slow request was not kept.
failureModes.mitigation: Tail sampling that keeps all errors and high-latency traces.
NTP discipline; trust parent-child structure over raw timestamps.

data.label: Dashboards & Exploration

input.name: Queries
input.type: Metrics, logs, and traces for one service and time

responsibilities: Shows service health against SLOs at a glance.
Lets engineers pivot between signals with one click.
Hosts runbooks linked from alerts.

failureModes.impact: Nobody finds the right one mid-incident.
failureModes.mitigation: Standard per-service dashboards generated from templates.

failureModes.impact: The whole stack slows when it is needed most.
failureModes.mitigation: Query limits, recording rules, and pre-aggregated views.
